statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 5 of 100 in the low band, twenty points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 57 in the elevated band on a Saudi East-West pipeline that remains shut with no restart date, WTI near $100.05, contested control at Bab al-Mandeb and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 87 percent for an increase. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources this hour, including one new verified weekend report.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, yet finished about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a round trip that retraced in both directions. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, fifteen hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one. Stress remains elevated and is described here as an environment reading only: under the fixed repository mapping it does not alter the mapped state.
headline: A third hour of a shut weekend tape leaves the Nasdaq-100 at its 29,368.44 close and VIX at 15.84, while the one new verified weekend item is ground escalation rather than market transmission: Yemeni government airstrikes near Mokha, with the Saudi East-West pipeline still shut and Monday's Salalah meeting on Hormuz shipping unchanged beyond this window.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources. The Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 settle, a round trip in which mean reversion worked in both directions. The broader tape agreed, with the Dow up 0.98% to 52,573.29, the S&P 500 up 0.86% to 7,656.98 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.96% to 26,333.04, each snapping a losing streak while still finishing the week lower. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having closed near the low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range.

The macro set behind that path is hawkish rather than disorderly. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, both in line, with core at 0.3% on the month, one tenth above consensus. Friday's live coverage reported roughly 87% priced for a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September meeting, against about 72% the previous day and 50% a week earlier. Treasury yields are firm, with the H.15 series re-checked this hour still showing the 10 September observation: the 2-year at 4.56%, the 5-year at 4.75%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%. A firm but broadly in-line print that still allowed a 459-point round trip is evidence of orderly price discovery, which is why the event continues to raise Stress and not Tail.

One verified item is new this hour, and it is ground escalation rather than market transmission. Yemen's internationally recognised government announced airstrikes on Houthi positions inside a declared zone near Mokha, with warnings to avoid the Taiz-Mokha and Mokha-Dhubab roads, after Houthi forces completed their push along Yemen's Red Sea coast on Friday and took Mocha, Dhubab and the island of Perim at the Bab al-Mandeb entrance. The Saudi position is unchanged: the Energy Ministry's East-West pipeline, a 1,200-kilometre route normally carrying 4 to 5 million barrels per day around the Strait of Hormuz, remains shut as a precaution after drone strikes that both Riyadh and Baghdad attributed to launches from Iraqi territory, and wire reporting updated at 03:24 UTC today still carries no restart date. Against that, crude eased rather than extended: WTI settled near $100.05, down 2.37%, and Brent near $104.61, down 2.81%, after Iran confirmed it will meet Gulf states and Iraqi representatives in Salalah, Oman on Monday to discuss Hormuz shipping. Stress therefore holds at 57 rather than rising.

The shared cross-asset collector last refreshed at 05:11 UTC and now sits well outside its 90-minute freshness window, so it is treated as stale background and supports no conclusion here. Its calendar feed was already unavailable, so the calendar below rests on independently verified sources and was re-checked this hour against the published United States economic calendar; one previously listed speaking engagement and two low-importance items were dropped because they could not be re-verified at that standard. What the stale file had shown remains consistent with the verified picture: Friday's advance was broad but internally dispersed, with seven of eight tracked megacaps higher on a mean near 0.94%, semiconductors uneven as ARM rose 4.17% while NVDA finished fractionally lower, and Treasury futures modestly lower in line with firm yields. Dispersion of that kind is the opposite of the single-direction alignment that precedes mean-reversion failure.

The decisive fact for this horizon stays mechanical. CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, fifteen hours after the last slot of this forecast. Every one of the twenty-four forward hours therefore describes a market in which no Nasdaq-100 price can print, so no persistent one-way path, no failed retracement and no session extreme can form. Conditional Tail is held at a low residual that steps from 5 to a 10 cap across the horizon, tracking accumulated unpriced weekend headline exposure ahead of an eventual reopen rather than any observed structure. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 08:00 UTC on 11 September to 07:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens in a trend-up read through the European hours, with Tail between 13 and 15 as the advance extended. The 12:30 UTC inflation print produced the only elevated readings of the window, Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode with Confidence cut to 70 and then 80 while the post-release path was still forming. Tail fell back to 15 within ninety minutes as NQ retraced, held between 15 and 17 through the U.S. afternoon in mixed mode, then fell to 13 and 7 around the 21:00 UTC halt. The final ten slots sit at Tail 5 to 6 in normal mode, tracking the closure rather than a directional view, while Stress decayed steadily from 83 to 57 as the event passed and volatility fell.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, fifteen hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 5 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps to 6, 7, 8 and 9 at roughly five-hour intervals before capping at 10 in the final four slots as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout. Stress runs 57 to a 61 ceiling and describes the environment rather than a path: a Saudi East-West pipeline outage whose latest update still carries no restart date, WTI near $100.05, contested control at Bab al-Mandeb qualified by Friday's easing in crude, Monday's Salalah meeting on Hormuz shipping and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 87 percent for an increase. Confidence decays from 85 to a 78 floor as the verified evidence set ages without any live price path to refresh it. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one.
